title: feat(plugin-security): one business sentence per built-in permission set, translated
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X1tNqzSWRgqddaNpX6CJvVQ)_

Fixes #25967

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## What changes

Setup → Permission Sets lists the platform's own permission sets next to every app's. Five of them showed no description. The no-bypass organization admin set and the three MCP agent sets showed text written for platform engineers. So an administrator choosing a set could not tell an administrator set from a member set.

Each of the nine sets in `defaultPermissionSets` now has one plain sentence (at most 160 characters, in the voice of objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2303) saying who holds it and what it opens or withholds. The engineering detail from the old no-bypass and MCP descriptions now lives in code comments beside each set. The ADR-0105 D4 / finding F2 note stays in the comment, so the string names no decision id.

| Set | Description (en) |
| --- | --- |
| `admin_full_access` | Platform operators: read and change every record in every organization, manage all users and settings, and author apps in Studio. |
| `organization_admin` | Owners and admins of an organization: full control of its records and members in Setup, but no app authoring or platform-wide settings. |
| `organization_admin_no_bypass` | Organization admins on a deployment with no wall between organizations: the same administration, but only the records their ownership and sharing open. |
| `member_default` | Every signed-in member's baseline: their own profile, keys and inbox and the member directory; business records come from their other sets. |
| `viewer_readonly` | Read-only users: read records across every object, as far as sharing allows, but create, edit or delete nothing. |
| `external_default` | People from outside the organization, such as customers or suppliers: their own profile and records, plus only what is shared with them. |
| `mcp_agent_data_read` | AI assistants a user connects with read access: they read what that user can read and change nothing. |
| `mcp_agent_data_write` | AI assistants a user connects with read and write access: they read and change what that user can, except user and sign-in data. |
| `mcp_agent_restricted` | AI assistants a user connects without data access: they can run the actions they were allowed, but read or change no record. |

**Translations.** zh-CN, ja-JP and es-ES (the three locales this plugin's bundle already carries) get each sentence through the `permissions.NAME.description` group that #25652 added. `translatePermissionSet` overlays it on `GET /meta/permission`. The entries are hand-authored in `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/translations/permission-sets.ts` and merged into `SecurityTranslations`. The generated `*.objects.generated.ts` files are not touched. No set's grants, name or label changed.

**Files:** `default-permission-sets.ts` (descriptions and comments), `translations/permission-sets.ts` (new), `translations/index.ts` (merge), `objects/permission-set-descriptions.test.ts` (new pin), `objects/default-permission-sets.test.ts` (the admin capability pin now leaves the copy out of its comparison), one `patch` changeset.

## Evidence

Live read, `pnpm dev:crm -- --fresh` built from head `a42ae5be`, signed in as the seeded admin. This is `GET /api/v1/meta/permission?scope=environment`, the list behind `/apps/setup/metadata/permission`. With `Accept-Language: zh-CN` it serves, for example:

- `organization_admin`: 组织的所有者和管理员：在设置中全面管理本组织的记录和成员，但不能构建应用或修改平台级设置。
- `viewer_readonly`: 只读用户：在共享允许的范围内查看所有对象的记录，但不能新建、编辑或删除任何内容。

All nine built-in sets served their zh-CN sentence and, under `en`, their English sentence. The CRM example declares only `en` and `zh-CN` (`GET /api/v1/i18n/locales`), so ja-JP was read on `pnpm dev:todo -- --fresh` (it declares ja-JP), and all nine ja-JP sentences were served. No example declares es-ES, so es-ES is pinned at unit level only. I did not build the console in this container, so there is no browser screenshot. The REST read above is the list the page renders.

## Tests (head `a42ae5be`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security test`: Test Files 224 passed (224), Tests 4741 passed, 45 skipped. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security typecheck`: exit 0.
- New pin `permission-set-descriptions.test.ts`: every set carries one sentence (no line break, at most 160 characters, one closing full stop, no code span, no set id), no two sets share a description, and each translated locale carries exactly the nine sets with a translated sentence and no label.
- Ablation, run on the committed tree (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, then restored, blob hashes equal to HEAD):
  - renaming `viewer_readonly` in all three locale groups failed 6 tests;
  - deleting `viewer_readonly`'s source description failed 1 test.
- `default-permission-sets.test.ts` "parsed declaration deep-equals the pre-#11965 inline literal" went red when the admin set gained a description. It now compares the set without its `description`, which is copy, not capability. The capability literal is unchanged.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 69 families on `a42ae5be`. All 69 ran and every exit is 0. `--ran` reconciliation: 69 derived, 69 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN. `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` first exited 3 because the checkout is shallow. It exited 0 after fetching its positive-control commit. `pnpm check:i18n` reported all bundles in sync. Scoped `eslint --no-inline-config packages/plugins/plugin-security` exited 0. CI runs everything else.

## Acceptance notes

- **Why the translations are hand-authored, not generated.** This plugin's extract runs objects-only, and stack mode needs a flag spelling that the `check:i18n` docstring harvester (`scripts/i18n-bundle-surface.mjs`) does not recognise. Generating the group would have meant changing that tooling and renaming the four generated exports. I kept to the claim's file surface and did neither. The cost is that no provenance table judges these entries. If a source sentence changes later, its three translations go stale silently unless the same change re-translates them. The file header says so. The new pin catches a missing or English-copy entry, not a stale one.
- **Labels stay untranslated.** Labels were out of scope under the ruling. The zh-CN read above serves `Administrator — Full Access` next to the app's own `CRM 销售用户`. This is reported to the seat, not fixed here.
- Main moved 12 commits after the branch point. None touch `plugin-security` or the translation code, and `git merge-tree` merges cleanly. I did not merge main.
- No other open PR touches `default-permission-sets.ts` or `plugin-security/src/translations/` (all 40 open PRs read at pr_create).
